clue.text: A turbulent river reach

indicators.note: turbulent water churns about, so the letters of river are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough stretch of river water.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to get there, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Station in old Jerusalem?

parts.note: reads like a railway stop in the ancient city, but means one of the Stations of the Cross, the hill of the crucifixion outside the walls

explanation.definitionFit: Calvary, the crucifixion site, is a Station of the Cross in the devotional sequence, located outside ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Small boy put in the high chair

indicators.note: the boy's name is placed inside the three letters of the word the

parts.note: taken as written
Ron is a short form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A little lad is lifted into his high chair at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The high chair is not a baby's seat but a monarch's raised seat of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial seat is raised on a dais, literally a high chair of state.

clue.text: Please make reparation

definitions.meaning: to please someone is to content them
to make amends, to pay off a debt or claim

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to gratify someone and to discharge an obligation in full.

clue.text: Bird nuts

definitions.meaning: a European bird famous for laying eggs in others' nests

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a bird species and slang for being crazy.

clue.text: Edited fifty diaries of Victorian novelist

indicators.note: edited material has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An editor working through fifty diaries of a nineteenth-century writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' rearranges L plus DIARIES. The prime minister also wrote novels such as Sybil.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli, Victoria's prime minister, wrote novels such as Sybil and Coningsby.

clue.text: The point of a quarrel?

parts.note: seems to ask what an argument is about, but a quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, whose tip is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a crossbow bolt, and its sharpened tip is the pointed head of the missile.

clue.text: Maurice has a heart of gold

indicators.note: the heart of the name Maurice is its inside, everything but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Maurice is a kind, generous man with a heart of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin aurum, so it means relating to or containing gold.

clue.text: Dosing is a remedy in the doctor's opinion

indicators.note: a remedy puts things right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor deciding that a dose of medicine will cure the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' rearranges DOSING IS A; it looks like the medicine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is a physician's judgement of what illness a patient has.

clue.text: Risk involved with a novice heard playing the bagpipes

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of Risk are mixed

parts.note: L is the learner plate sign, a novice driver

explanation.surface: A beginner piper takes a risk performing in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges RISK into SKIR; L is the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill wailing sound bagpipes make, so it is what is heard when they play.

clue.text: Slight legato effect

definitions.meaning: in music, a curved mark joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an insult, and in music the curved mark binding notes to be played smoothly.

clue.text: Make firm pay up

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to establish something securely and to pay off what is owed.

clue.text: Someone very fond of a Cornish river trip?

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England's south-western county
a lover is someone devoted to a thing

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keen on boat excursions along a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey, but it means stumble. The Fal flows through Cornwall to Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to stumble and tumble to the ground, an everyday phrasal verb.

clue.text: Feeling guilty, so has made amends

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so the letters of has made are changed around

explanation.surface: Someone full of remorse who has tried to make up for wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amends' rearranges HAS MADE; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed and full of remorse over a wrong feels guilty.

clue.text: Running out of stock, all at once

definitions.text: Running out of stock, all at once

parts.words: Running out of stock, all at once
parts.note: sounds like a shop selling out, but stock here is livestock, cattle charging in a panic together

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd of cattle, all running together at once.

clue.text: Feel jealous of minister who lacks nothing

indicators.note: the diplomat lacks something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic minister
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A government minister with nothing resents others' wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet what another person has is to resent them out of jealousy.

clue.text: Desperate doctor takes wine cold

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A doctor in a bad way resorts to chilled wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures are extreme ones, the same sense as drastic.

clue.text: Pinch your old-fashioned secret

parts.note: to pinch is slang for steal
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or covert, so done in secret.

clue.text: Checker of drawing

definitions.meaning: a piece in the board game checkers
pulling, as of a load or of air, or of beer from a cask

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; draught also means the act of drawing or pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a draughts piece is a checker, and the noun also means pulling a load or drawing beer.

clue.text: Transfer worker to deliveries

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
in cricket an over is a set of six balls, or deliveries

explanation.surface: A worker moved to the deliveries department.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled, each one a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the passing of responsibility or control from one party to another.

clue.text: Order posted by tyrant

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of posted are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A command is pinned up by a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a synonym for tyrant.

clue.text: Suitable voice for a high score?

definitions.text: Suitable voice for a high score?

parts.words: Suitable voice for a high score?
parts.note: a musical score written high suits a boy soprano, and in darts the inner ring triples a high score

explanation.definitionFit: The highest singing voice, apt for music pitched up, also names the darts ring that triples points.

clue.text: It's not intended for the understanding of our betters

definitions.text: It's not intended for the understanding of our betters

parts.words: It's not intended for the understanding of our betters
parts.note: seems to be about social superiors, but betters are people who bet, and bookmakers' hand-signal code is meant to be private

explanation.walkthrough: Racecourse bookmakers signal odds to one another with arm movements, a code punters are not meant to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' secret system of arm signals for passing odds at a racecourse, opaque to punters.

clue.text: It conceals the seamy side of our habits

definitions.text: It conceals the seamy side of our habits

parts.words: It conceals the seamy side of our habits
parts.note: reads like hiding bad behaviour, but habits are garments and the seamy side is literally the inside with seams

explanation.definitionFit: The inner layer of fabric sewn into a coat covers the raw seams of the garment.

clue.text: Health resorts get a number fit

parts.note: spas are resorts for health cures
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Visitors to health resorts get a good number of them fit again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy, but here it is a noun, a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit is a sudden convulsion or seizure of the muscles.

clue.text: Assault course may be the point of the joke

parts.note: a punch is a blow, an assault
a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: An army assault course may be where a comedian finds humour.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line of a gag delivers its humour, the crux of the joke.

clue.text: Poem being performed in Greek theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a play that is on is being staged

explanation.surface: A poem being recited in an ancient Greek amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The odeon was a roofed building in ancient Greece for musical performances and recitals.

clue.text: Object about unrestrained punishment

indicators.note: the word for an object goes around the other piece

parts.note: a thing is an object
rash means reckless, unrestrained

explanation.surface: A protest about harsh, excessive punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but it is the noun THING.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating given as a punishment, especially a severe one.
